title: Commercial and HOA Turf in Evans, CO | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Evans code says artificial turf is not acceptable for public or common areas. An April 2026 ordinance adds the state's landscaping rules; its text isn't online.
h1: Evans's landscape code, rewritten in 2023, already said artificial turf is not acceptable for public or common areas before Colorado's ban took effect.

display.paint: not acceptable for public or common areas

lede: The chapter it sits in governs HOA common ground in new subdivisions, new site plans, apartments, nonresidential buildings and parking lots. In April 2026 the council added a section to carry out the state's landscaping mandates, and its text is not in the online code yet. Not legal advice. Checked September 25, 2026.

answer.question: Can an Evans HOA or business install artificial turf?
answer.answer: Not on public or common areas the city reviews, under the published code: Evans's landscape chapter says artificial turf is not acceptable there. Ordinance 858-26, passed April 21, 2026, adds a section implementing state landscaping mandates that may treat functional turf differently, so ask Evans Planning. NoCo Turf Co. installs commercial and HOA turf in Evans, Colorado.

blocks.h2: Section 18.08.020 sets a stricter line than the state: no artificial turf on public or common areas.
blocks.takeaway: Colorado's law allows functional turf; the Evans sentence names no exception.
paras: The sentence sits in the unbuilt-areas rule of the landscape chapter Evans adopted through Ord. 804-23 on October 17, 2023. It reaches the common and public areas of any new subdivision, new or substantially amended site plans, new or substantially improved multifamily and nonresidential buildings, new or improved parking lots, and infill and rehabilitation of existing sites, where the Director may prorate the standards to the part being worked on.

Colorado's rule, in force since January 1, 2026, bars nonfunctional artificial turf in new development and redevelopment on commercial, institutional and industrial property, HOA common property, and street rights-of-way, parking lots and medians, and keeps playgrounds, sports fields, picnic grounds, parts of parks and golf greens allowed. A full-text search of the Evans code as codified through January 6, 2026 finds the word nonfunctional nowhere. Not legal advice.

On April 21, 2026 the council passed Ord. 858-26, adding Section 18.08.080 to implement state-mandated landscaping requirements. Municode lists it as not yet codified, and its text was not available for this page. It may bring in the state's functional categories or leave the 2023 sentence standing as the stricter local rule; it depends on that text, so ask Evans Planning for the adopted ordinance before a board or owner plans turf.

blocks.h2: New Evans subdivisions owe common open space, and new parks owe ball fields, playgrounds or courts.
paras: Residential subdivisions over 5 acres or 20 units set aside common open space at 4 acres per 1,000 people. Commercial subdivisions set aside 5% of the site under 5 acres, 8% from 5 to 20 acres and 12% above that. Inside a new park, 15% to 50% of the area goes to active recreation such as ball fields, playgrounds or sport courts, and multifamily projects over 12 units owe common areas of their own.

All of it is designed under the landscape chapter, which also tells designers to keep high-irrigation turf to high-use areas with high visibility and functional needs and to use water-conserving or drought-tolerant grasses. On the published text, that points new Evans ball fields and play lawns toward living grass.

Existing city fields include Riverside Park's four ball fields, two of them lighted, and Ridge Park's soccer-sized open turf area. The park descriptions don't say whether any of those surfaces is artificial.

blocks.h2: Evans makes new subdivisions build non-potable irrigation for every lot and common area.
paras: In areas the City Council designates, Section 13.06.010 requires new development to build a non-potable irrigation system for all lots and common areas, dedicate enough water rights to run it, and turn the system and the water over to the City.

That is the kind of system the 2026 drought reached. After the Greeley-Loveland Irrigation Company said its deliveries would end after August 28, city-run non-potable irrigation outside The Ridge at Prairie View and Willowbrook moved to potable water, billed at potable rates; the [Evans turf page](/areas/evans-co/) has the details.

Metro districts carry some of that load. Liberty Draw Metropolitan Districts 1 through 9 had a service-plan amendment before the council on July 21, 2026, and the Liberty Draw architectural guidelines tie every home's exterior irrigation to the non-potable system. Colorado's turf law counts metro districts as local entities, so its ban binds them as it binds the city.

faq.q: Can an Evans HOA keep the artificial turf it already has?
faq.a: Colorado's law lets a local government allow turf installed before January 1, 2026 to be maintained, and Evans's published code doesn't address existing turf. Its landscape chapter does reach rehabilitation of existing sites, so a full replacement may count. It depends on the project; ask Evans Planning before the board votes.

faq.q: Does the state's redevelopment test apply in Evans?
faq.a: The state's ban reaches redevelopment, meaning a project that needs a building or landscaping permit, plan check or design review and disturbs more than 50% of the landscape area. Evans's own chapter names infill and rehabilitation of existing sites, with no percentage threshold, and lets the Director prorate. Which governs a given site depends on Section 18.08.080; ask Evans Planning.

faq.q: Can an Evans apartment complex put its dog relief area on turf?
faq.a: Evans lists a dog relief area among the features multifamily common areas can include, but those common areas fall under the landscape chapter's sentence on artificial turf. Colorado adds its own date: from January 1, 2028, the state ban reaches common areas of multifamily properties with more than 12 units. Until Section 18.08.080 is read, it depends: ask Evans Planning.
